name: Playing Not Spraying
rappels: Multiple rappels down the SE side of the peak; 70m rope recommended, bring extra webbing for building anchors
descent_text: Descend by making a series of rappels down the SE side of Silver Horn. A 70-meter rope is recommended, and carrying extra/bulk webbing is advisable since fixed rappel anchors are sparse and some anchors must be built from scratch.
approach: The Silver Horn is a sub-summit on the east ridge of Silver Star Mountain, east of the main summit, and both of its routes are on the clean white granite of its south face. That face is not reached from the Wine Spires pullout or Burgundy Col, which serve the other side of the crest. Instead, walk the Cedar Creek Trail from its trailhead at the end of FR 5310-200, off SR-20 about half a mile east of the Klipchuck Campground turnoff. After roughly five miles, turn off to the right below the old burn and follow a rough path up the right-hand side of the creek that drains the south side of the Silver Horn. Meadows at about 6,200 ft give good camping below the face.
overview: Playing Not Spraying (5.10, Grade III, 8 pitches, 800 ft) climbs the clean white granite south face of Silver Horn, a rarely-climbed sub-summit of Silver Star Mountain at Washington Pass.
beta: Opens with a layback off a large clean flake into a long left-facing corner system with finger cracks, crosses right below a roof into a splitter crack to a mid-route ledge, then a second roof leads to a hand crack and stemming corners with a hard exit, topping out via a deep summit chimney; protection is cams and nuts to 3 inches throughout.
